newsitem.title: USA: Mid Ocean adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Mid Ocean adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Bermuda-based reinsurer Mid Ocean Ltd has adopted a shareholder rights plan that would protect shareholders against unsolicited takeover offers.
The company said the plan, which would exempt the existing holdings of EXEL Ltd, which has a 29.8 percent stake in Mid Ocean.
"The rights are intended to enable all Mid Ocean shareholders to realize the long-term value of their investment in Mid Ocean," chief executive Michael Butt.
"They will not prevent a takeover of Mid Ocean. However, the rights plan should encourage anyone seeking to acquire Mid Oean to negotiate with the board prior to attempting a takeover," he said.
A Mid Ocean spokesman on Thursday declined comment on why the company decided to adopt the rights plan at this time.

However, the insurance industry has been among the hottest sectors in the merger market and the Bermuda market saw its first bidding war this summer when ACE Ltd and IPC Holdings Ltd made rival offers for Tempest Reinsurance Holdings Ltd.

Under the plan, each holder of ordinary shares at the close of business on October 1, 1996 will receive a distribution of one right for each class A ordinary share held. Each right entitles the holder to purchase from Mid Ocean one class A ordinary share at an initial purchase price of $140.

The rights will become exercisable and will detach from the class A ordinary shares a specified period of time after any person has become the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares.

They also will become exercisable and detach from the class A ordinary shares after any person has commended a tender of exchange offer, which if consummated, would result in any person becoming the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of the common shares.
Parties, such as EXEL, owning 20 percent or more of the common shares of Mid Ocean on the date the plan was adopted would not cause the rights to become exercisable.

If anyone becomes the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares, other than EXEL, each right will entitle the holder other than the acquiring person, to purchase for the then applicable price Mid Ocean common shares having a value of twice the purchase price.

If, following an acquisition of 20 percent or more of Mid Ocean's common shares, Mid Ocean is involved in certain mergers or other business combinations or sells or transfers more than 50 percent of its assets or earning power, each right will entitle the holder to purchase for the then applicable price common stock of the other party to such transaction having a value twice the purchase price.

At any time after a person has acquired 20 percent or more, but before anyone has acquired more than 50 percent, of the company's ordinary shares, Mid Ocean may exchange all or part of the rights for common shares at an exchange ratio of one class A ordinary share per right, subject to rights holders delivering to the company an amount in cash equal to the par value of each class A ordinary share to be received.

Mid Ocean may redeem the rights at a price of $0.01 per right at any time prior to a specified period of time after a person has become the beneficial owner of 20 percent or more of its common shares. The rights will expire on October 1, 2006, unless earlier exchanged or redeemed.
